criteria.justification: The operation uses only `addReview(productId: ID!, rating: Int!, body: String)` and Review fields `id, rating, body, createdAt, author`, with none of the flagged fabrications (no `reviewText`/`title`, no rating enum, no `updateReview`/`deleteReview`, no invented arguments).
The mutation body calls the operation by its exact name: `addReview(productId: $productId, rating: $rating, body: $body)`.
The variable declaration is `$productId: ID!` and it is passed as the `productId` argument identifying the product.
`$rating: Int!` is declared and typed as `rating: number` in TypeScript, not a string, enum, or float type.
`$body: String` is nullable and the wrapper takes `body?: string`, sending `body ?? null` when omitted.
The selection set is `id, rating, body, createdAt, author { ... }`, all of which are listed Review fields.
The request is made with `{ authenticated: true }` via the client's authenticated path, and the doc comment notes it acts "on behalf of the signed-in customer."
